BUSINESS CONTEXT:
- Hyperlocal Grocery Delivery Quick Commerce (Q-Commerce) Aggregator Model with gig-economy logistics; monetized through transaction commissions, delivery fees, subscriptions, advert...
BUSINESS OPERATING MODEL:
- Hyperlocal, ultra-fast (typically under 60 minutes) delivery of fresh perishables and daily essentials, relying on a dense network of micro-fulfillment centers rather than centrali...
BUSINESS PRODUCT SERVICE:
- Hyperlocal last-mile delivery of physical goods
- Algorithmic routing and order allocation services
- Data analytics and advertising services derived from transaction data
- Real-time access to aggregated grocery inventory via digital interface
BUSINESS OUTCOME:
- Satisfied customers with high ratings and repeat usage
- Regulatory compliance and risk mitigation
- Successful order fulfillment within target timeframes (e.g., <60 mins)
- Accurate inventory availability and reduced overselling
- Optimized revenue streams and cost control
- Efficient utilization of store staff and delivery agents
BUSINESS FUNCTION:
- Compliance and regulatory adherence
- Customer relationship and support
- Financial settlement and revenue management
- Inventory synchronization and validation
- Order orchestration and allocation
- Marketplace aggregation and catalog management
- Logistics coordination and fulfillment
BUSINESS MONETIZATION MODEL:
- Aggregating fragmented inventory from hyperlocal stores into a unified digital interface, optimizing last-mile logistics through algorithmic routing, and enabling real-time order f...
BUSINESS LIFECYCLE STAGE:
- Order Preparation Allocation confirmation. Store personnel pick items, verify quality, pack for transport, and hand over to the delivery partner.
- Financial Settlement Handover confirmation. Transaction is finalized, funds are transferred to the customer, and revenue share is settled between the platform and the store.
- Operational Readiness Acquisition of sufficient initial inventory and confirmed delivery partner availability. Testing logistics routes, calibrating demand forecasting models, and ...
- Post-Transaction Review Completion of settlement. Collection of feedback, rating of experience, and initiation of loyalty points accrual.
- Order Initiation Customer action on the digital interface. Customer expresses need, browses available catalog, selects items, and submits a request for immediate fulfillment.
- Handover & Confirmation Arrival at customer location. Customer receives the order, verifies contents, and confirms receipt via the platform.
- Supply Chain Integration Completion of partner contracts and initial inventory data ingestion. Onboarding stores, defining SKU catalogs, mapping inventory locations, and establishi...
- Last-Mile Delivery Pickup confirmation from the store. Delivery partner picks up the order, navigates to the customer location, and completes the physical transfer.
- Order Validation & Allocation Successful submission of the order request. System validates inventory availability, calculates fees, confirms delivery slot, and allocates the order ...
- Foundation Establishment Strategic decision to launch a new market zone or service category. Defining the service area, selecting store partners, establishing logistics partnership...
- Lifecycle Conclusion Completion of all feedback and settlement processes. The specific order instance is closed; data is archived for analytics; optional dispute resolution window ...
ACTOR DEFINITION:
- Payment Provider: Financial institution that processes customer transactions and facilitates fund transfers.
- Fulfillment Supervisor: Store staff member who coordinates the picking, packing, and handover of orders to delivery partners...
- Platform Operator: Entity that manages the digital interface, orchestrates order allocation, and settles financial tran...
- Customer: End user who initiates orders, selects items, and confirms delivery completion.
- Delivery Partner: Independent agent or gig-worker responsible for last-mile logistics and physical handover of goods.
- Store Partner: Physical retail location that provides inventory, staff for order picking, and fulfillment capabilit...
- Order Allocation Engine: Automated system component that validates inventory, calculates fees, and assigns orders to specific...
- Merchandiser: Personnel at stores who pack orders and verify item quality before dispatch.
- Regulatory Authority: External body that enforces food safety standards and labor laws applicable to the service.
BUSINESS OBJECT:
- Delivery Assignment
- Store Partner Agreement
- Product Catalog
- Delivery Zone Map
- Feedback Record
- Order Request
- Fulfillment Task
- Dispute Ticket
- Customer Profile
- Service Area Definition
- Financial Transaction Record
- Delivery Proof
- Real-Time Inventory Snapshot
- Assigned Delivery Slot
BUSINESS ASSUMPTION:
- Real-time inventory synchronization between the physical store and the digital platform is technically feasible and reliable

frs.requirement: The system shall maintain synchronized, real-time inventory levels across all Store/Fulfillment Centers to prevent overselling of perishable goods and ensure accurate stock visibility.
frs.need: The business requires immediate stock accuracy to prevent selling items that are out of stock or expired, thereby protecting revenue and maintaining customer trust.
rules: Stock quantities must be locked exclusively to a single Order Request until the fulfillment task is completed or the order is cancelled.
Perishable items must be prioritized for allocation to orders based on their proximity to the expiration date.
The system must flag a synchronization discrepancy if the data link latency exceeds the defined threshold or if a sync failure is detected.
Locked stock must be automatically released if the Order Request is not confirmed within the allocated time window.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically assign incoming orders to the nearest Store Partner that has sufficient Real-Time Inventory Snapshot and available capacity.
frs.need: The business requires instant, optimal allocation of orders to physical nodes to minimize delivery time and prevent inventory overselling.
rules: An order must only be assigned to a store if the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot shows available quantity greater than or equal to the requested quantity for all items.
If no store has sufficient inventory for the complete order, the system must not assign the order and must flag it for manual review.
The system must prioritize the nearest store based on the shortest estimated preparation and dispatch time.
Inventory quantities reserved by an automatic assignment must be immediately deducted from the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot to prevent overselling.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable Delivery Partners to view, accept, and manage their assigned delivery slots while ensuring dynamic agent assignment and capacity verification.
frs.need: The business needs to optimize last-mile logistics by ensuring the right agent receives orders based on real-time capacity and workload status.
rules: A delivery slot cannot be assigned to an agent if their current workload exceeds the maximum capacity defined for their service zone.
An agent must explicitly accept a delivery assignment before the system confirms the slot as active.
Dynamic reassignment of a delivery task is only permitted if the original agent rejects the task or exceeds capacity limits.
The system must recalculate estimated arrival times if traffic patterns change significantly after the initial assignment.

frs.requirement: The system shall capture and verify digital proof of delivery via direct input or external API retrieval before releasing funds.
frs.need: The business needs irrefutable evidence of physical handover to close the logistics loop and trigger financial settlement securely.
rules: Funds shall not be released until a valid delivery proof is recorded in the system.
Proof retrieved via external API shall be treated with the same verification standards as locally captured proof.
A Dispute Ticket shall be created if the delivery proof lacks a timestamp or valid signature.
The system shall reject delivery proof if the associated Delivery Assignment is marked as cancelled.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically calculate and distribute transaction revenue to the Platform Operator, Store Partner, and Payment Provider immediately upon delivery confirmation.
frs.need: The business needs to ensure accurate, transparent, and timely financial settlement for all parties involved in a transaction to maintain trust and operational efficiency.
rules: Financial distribution shall only occur after a valid Delivery Proof is recorded.
The sum of all distributed amounts must equal the total value of the Financial Transaction Record.
Transactions involving high-risk indicators must be paused for manual verification before settlement.
Settlement calculations must strictly adhere to the terms defined in the Store Partner Agreement.
A Financial Transaction Record must be generated for every completed delivery regardless of outcome.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate real-time alerts for inventory items approaching their shelf-life limits to prioritize fulfillment or trigger removal.
frs.need: The business needs to minimize waste and maintain product quality by proactively managing perishable stock before it becomes unsellable.
rules: An item is considered 'nearing expiry' if its remaining shelf life is less than the configured safety margin.
New Order Requests must be rejected if the primary fulfillment source contains items flagged as 'nearing expiry'.
The system must update the Product Catalog status immediately upon detecting an expiry alert.
All expiry alerts must be logged with a timestamp and the specific item identifier.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically generate and track a Dispute Ticket when a Delivery Proof indicates a missing item, damage, or failed delivery.
frs.need: The business needs an automated mechanism to capture exceptions early, ensuring fair resolution and accurate financial adjustments without manual intervention.
rules: A Dispute Ticket must be created immediately upon receipt of a Delivery Proof indicating a delivery exception.
The Dispute Ticket status must transition from 'Open' to 'Resolved' only after a final decision is recorded.
A Dispute Ticket must remain linked to the original Order Request for the duration of the resolution process.
Financial adjustments cannot be finalized until the Dispute Ticket is marked as Resolved.

frs.requirement: The system shall retrieve, validate, and store external regulatory licenses and food safety certifications for Store Partners to ensure legal operation.
frs.need: The business needs to mitigate legal risks and maintain trust by ensuring all Store Partners operate within required regulatory boundaries.
rules: A Store Partner must have a valid and non-expired food safety certificate to accept new orders.
The system must block order allocation to a Store Partner if their primary operating license is flagged as invalid.
Regulatory compliance status must be updated within 24 hours of receiving new data from external sources.
A Store Partner must be notified immediately if their license expiration date is within 30 days.

frs.requirement: The system shall manage the full lifecycle of the Customer Profile, enabling the creation, modification, and archival of identity and preference records throughout the customer's engagement.
frs.need: The business needs a centralized, accurate record of customer identity and preferences to ensure secure order routing, accurate financial settlement, and personalized service delivery.
rules: A Customer Profile must contain a unique identifier before any Order Request can be associated with it.
Contact details within a Customer Profile must be verified before the profile status is set to active.
Archived Customer Profiles must retain all historical data and cannot be modified after the archival action is confirmed.
Any modification to a Customer Profile must be timestamped and attributed to the actor performing the change.

frs.requirement: The system shall manage the full lifecycle of Store Partner Agreements, enabling the creation, amendment, and historical tracking of commercial terms while controlling access to these documents.
frs.need: The business needs to maintain legally binding, auditable records of commercial terms to ensure operational compliance and accurate financial settlements with store partners.
rules: An amendment to an active agreement must immediately create a new version number while marking the previous version as historical.
A Store Partner Agreement must be marked as 'Active' before any associated Order Requests can be allocated to that partner.
Access to edit an agreement version is restricted to the Platform Operator and the Store Partner associated with that agreement.
The system must prevent the deletion of any agreement version once it has been created.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable the Merchandiser to create, update, and archive product catalog entries while enforcing data validation and version control.
frs.need: The business needs a structured way to manage product lifecycle data to ensure accurate inventory representation and prevent overselling.
rules: A product entry cannot be updated if it is in an archived state.
All product updates must include a timestamp and the identifier of the user making the change.
Required fields such as product name and price must be populated before a new entry is created.
Previous versions of a product must be retained and marked as archived when a new version is published.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable the Platform Operator to create, modify, and version geospatial service area definitions and travel time matrices to ensure accurate delivery feasibility and pricing.
frs.need: The business needs this to dynamically restrict order acceptance to feasible areas and calculate accurate delivery fees based on real-time traffic and route constraints.
rules: A new version of a Service Area Definition must supersede the previous active version immediately upon publication.
Orders originating from addresses outside the active Service Area Definition must be rejected by the Order Allocation Engine.
Travel time matrices must be recalculated whenever a Service Area Definition is modified to reflect updated route constraints.
All modifications to Service Area Definitions must be logged with a timestamp and the identity of the Platform Operator.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable the secure creation, retention, and long-term archival of detailed financial ledgers and settlement records for all monetary exchanges.
frs.need: The business needs immutable financial records to ensure accurate revenue sharing, support regulatory audits, and provide verifiable evidence for dispute resolution.
rules: A financial transaction record must include item costs, delivery fees, taxes, platform commissions, and net settlement amounts to be considered complete.
The system must link a financial transaction record to verifiable evidence of delivery before finalizing the settlement status.
Any deviation from the standard process must be recorded with the nature of the issue and the current resolution status.
Contractual details including commission rates and payout schedules must be archived alongside the financial transaction record.

frs.requirement: The system shall manage the full lifecycle of Service Area Definitions, enabling the creation, activation, deactivation, and historical tracking of geographically delimited delivery zones.
frs.need: The business requires precise control over operational boundaries to ensure orders are only accepted and fulfilled within feasible geographic limits.
rules: A Service Area Definition must be in an active state before it can be used to validate new Order Requests.
Any modification to an active Service Area Definition must be logged with the reason for change and the identity of the operator.
Deactivation of a Service Area Definition must immediately prevent the acceptance of new orders originating from that zone.
A Service Area Definition cannot be created if its geographic boundaries overlap with a restricted zone defined by the Regulatory Authority.

frs.requirement: The system shall maintain an immutable chronological history of all status transitions for every Delivery Assignment from creation to final closure.
frs.need: The business needs this to provide full auditability of the delivery lifecycle, enabling root cause analysis for delays and verifying compliance with service level agreements.
rules: A status transition is only valid if the new status logically follows the previous status in the defined lifecycle.
The system must record a status entry for every state change, regardless of whether the change was manual or automated.
Historical status records must remain read-only and cannot be modified after creation.
The history log must include the timestamp in the system's standard time zone.

frs.requirement: The system shall enforce role-based access control by granting or denying system actions based on the specific permissions assigned to each actor.
frs.need: The business needs to restrict system access to ensure data security, operational integrity, and compliance with internal governance policies.
rules: An actor may only perform an action if their assigned role includes the specific permission for that action.
Access attempts by actors without the required permission must be denied and recorded in an audit log.
Permission changes must take effect immediately for all subsequent access requests.
Actors cannot bypass role-based restrictions through direct data manipulation.

frs.requirement: The system shall enforce multi-factor authentication for all Delivery Partners accessing the delivery agent mobile application to verify identity before granting access to operational tools.
frs.need: The business requires secure verification to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive customer data and delivery instructions by malicious actors impersonating gig-workers.
rules: Access is granted only when both the primary credential and the secondary verification code are valid and match.
A failed authentication attempt triggers an immediate lockout if the total number of consecutive failures exceeds the system threshold.
The secondary verification code expires after a short duration to prevent reuse.
Authentication logs must be immutable and retained for the duration of the regulatory compliance period.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable Store Partner personnel to validate item quality against the order request before marking the fulfillment task as complete.
frs.need: The business needs this to prevent shipping defective or incorrect items, thereby reducing returns and maintaining customer trust.
rules: A Fulfillment Task cannot transition to a 'Ready for Dispatch' status unless a quality verification record exists for every item.
If a quality check fails for any item, the system must flag the Fulfillment Task as 'Requires Correction' and block dispatch.
The system must display the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot alongside the Order Request to facilitate accurate physical verification.

frs.requirement: The system shall validate customer identity and contact details during the onboarding process to ensure compliance and secure account creation.
frs.need: The business needs to verify customer identity to prevent fraud, ensure accurate delivery routing, and maintain regulatory compliance before allowing order placement.
rules: A Customer Profile cannot be activated until identity verification is successful.
Contact details must match the name and address on the verified identity document.
Any failed verification attempt must generate a Dispute Ticket for manual review.
The system must flag accounts with inconsistent contact details for further investigation.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate an immutable audit log for every action performed by authorized actors to satisfy external regulatory compliance requirements.
frs.need: The business needs this to provide verifiable proof of operational adherence to labor, data privacy, and safety laws during regulatory inspections.
rules: Every log entry must be immutable and tamper-evident.
Audit logs must be retained for a period not shorter than the minimum legal requirement for the operating zone.
Only actions initiated by human actors or their direct digital representations shall be logged for compliance.
The audit log must be accessible to the Regulatory Authority upon request without delay.

frs.requirement: The system shall assign the authority to approve or reject a Dispute Ticket to a specific actor based on the ticket's origin, severity, and the involved partners.
frs.need: The business needs a clear, automated assignment of dispute resolution authority to ensure fair, timely, and legally compliant handling of customer claims.
rules: An actor cannot approve a Dispute Ticket where they are the accused party.
Disputes involving financial refunds must be approved by the Platform Operator.
Disputes regarding product quality must be approved by the Store Partner.
Disputes regarding delivery performance must be approved by the Delivery Partner.
Unresolved Dispute Tickets must be escalated to a Fulfillment Supervisor after the initial assignment deadline.

frs.requirement: The system shall prevent the submission of an Order Request if the calculated cart total is below the minimum order value defined in the Store Partner Agreement.
frs.need: The business needs this to ensure economic viability by preventing the processing of orders that cannot cover operational costs or meet delivery thresholds.
rules: An Order Request cannot be submitted if the sum of item prices is strictly less than the minimum order value defined in the Store Partner Agreement.
An Order Request can be submitted if the sum of item prices is equal to or greater than the minimum order value defined in the Store Partner Agreement.
The minimum order value must be dynamically retrieved from the Store Partner Agreement at the time of validation.
The system must display a clear error message to the Customer when the minimum order value is not met.

frs.requirement: The system shall prevent the creation of an Order Request if the customer's delivery address falls outside the active boundaries of any defined Service Area Definition.
frs.need: The business needs to enforce strict geofencing to ensure operational feasibility and prevent accepting orders that cannot be physically fulfilled within the hyperlocal zones.
rules: An order must not be created if the delivery address is geographically outside all active Service Area Definitions.
A Service Area Definition must be marked as active to allow order placement within its boundaries.
The system must validate the delivery address against the Service Area Definition at the moment of order submission.

frs.requirement: The system shall prevent the creation of an Order Request containing any Product Catalog item where the current date exceeds the item's expiry date or freshness threshold.
frs.need: The business needs to prevent the sale of expired or unsafe perishable goods to protect customer health and maintain regulatory compliance.
rules: An item is considered expired if the current date is later than the item's defined expiry date.
An Order Request must contain zero expired items to be successfully created.
Items flagged as expired must be immediately excluded from the available inventory snapshot.
The system must validate expiry status for all items in the cart before finalizing the order.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically calculate and apply the correct revenue share percentage to a Financial Transaction Record based on the active commission rate defined in the Store Partner Agreement.
frs.need: The business needs to ensure accurate and compliant revenue distribution between the platform and store partners by dynamically applying contractual commission rates to every financial settlement.
rules: The system shall use the commission rate from the most recently active Store Partner Agreement for any given transaction.
The system shall prevent the finalization of a Financial Transaction Record if no valid Store Partner Agreement exists for the involved Store Partner.
The system shall calculate the net settlement amount by subtracting the calculated commission from the gross revenue.
The system shall treat a Store Partner Agreement as inactive if its effective end date has passed or if it is explicitly marked as terminated.

frs.requirement: The system shall evaluate transaction patterns and consume third-party fraud detection services to assess risk scores for orders before processing.
frs.need: The business needs this to prevent financial loss from fraudulent transactions and ensure secure payment processing.
rules: An order must be flagged for manual review if the calculated risk score exceeds the high-risk threshold.
The system must consume the third-party fraud detection service response before allowing any financial transaction to proceed.
High-risk orders must remain in a pending state until a Payment Provider explicitly approves or rejects them.
All risk assessment events must be recorded with a timestamp and the specific indicators that triggered the score.

frs.requirement: The system shall securely connect with the Payment Provider to process customer payments, initiate fund transfers, and manage refunds or reversals for financial transactions.
frs.need: The business requires a secure financial integration to accurately monetize transactions, settle funds between parties, and protect against financial loss through fraud detection and reversal capabilities.
rules: A financial transaction cannot be finalized until the Payment Provider validates the payer's solvency.
Refunds or reversals must be initiated only after a valid request is received from an authorized actor.
The system must capture all monetary components (costs, fees, taxes, commissions) in the transaction record.
Final settlement amounts are contingent upon the verification of the Delivery Proof.

frs.requirement: The system shall ingest real-time operational data from external logistics providers to monitor fleet availability and route constraints.
frs.need: The business needs this to dynamically adjust delivery capacity and fees based on live network status, preventing service degradation during congestion.
rules: The system shall treat a data link latency exceeding the defined threshold as a network disruption.
The system shall invalidate an Assigned Delivery Slot if the external network status indicates a route constraint.
The system shall update the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot to mark items as unavailable if the logistics link is down.
The system shall prioritize agents with lower workload status when assigning tasks during network congestion.

frs.requirement: The system shall integrate with external mapping services to consume live traffic and road network data for calculating accurate delivery times.
frs.need: Accurate delivery time estimates are critical for setting realistic fees, managing customer expectations, and optimizing fleet capacity.
rules: The system shall use live traffic data to adjust estimated arrival times whenever congestion exceeds a predefined threshold.
The system shall reject any calculated route that falls outside the authorized Service Area Definition.
The system shall recalculate delivery times immediately upon receiving an update from the external mapping service.
The system shall display the estimated arrival time to the Delivery Partner and Customer within five minutes of the last data refresh.

frs.requirement: The system shall integrate with external tax services to dynamically calculate and remit applicable sales taxes for transactions within authorized service zones.
frs.need: The business needs this to ensure full regulatory compliance and accurate financial reporting across varying jurisdictions.
rules: The system shall not finalize an Order Request if the calculated tax rate exceeds the maximum threshold defined by the Regulatory Authority.
The system shall automatically generate a Dispute Ticket whenever a tax calculation error is detected during the Financial Transaction Record generation.
The system shall only apply tax rates from jurisdictions where the Service Area Definition confirms operational authorization.
The system shall update the Financial Transaction Record immediately upon receiving a new tax rate update from the external service.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically initiate a refund process when a dispute ticket is validated by the Regulatory Authority or when a delivery failure is confirmed by the Delivery Partner.
frs.need: The business needs to automate financial reversals to ensure customer trust and operational efficiency when service failures or validated disputes occur.
rules: A refund must be initiated only after a dispute ticket is marked as validated or a delivery failure is explicitly confirmed.
The refund amount must match the total value of the items in the original Order Request.
No new Delivery Assignment can be created for the same Order Request while a refund is in progress.
The system must capture the specific reason code for the refund initiation to support financial auditing.

frs.requirement: The system shall calculate and apply partial refunds for specific missing or damaged items within a valid Order Request based on verified inventory or delivery proof discrepancies.
frs.need: The business needs to automatically adjust financial obligations for customers when specific items in an order are unavailable or damaged, ensuring accurate billing and maintaining trust without requiring manual intervention for every discrepancy.
rules: A partial refund shall only be triggered if the discrepancy is confirmed by a Delivery Proof or a Real-Time Inventory Snapshot indicating unavailability.
The refund amount shall strictly equal the sum of the unit prices for the specific missing or damaged items, excluding any taxes or delivery fees.
A partial refund shall not be processed if the Order Request has already been fully refunded or cancelled.
The system shall prevent a partial refund calculation if the item in question is marked as permanently discontinued in the Product Catalog.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically reassign failed delivery tasks to available Delivery Partners based on proximity to the delivery address and current agent capacity.
frs.need: The business needs to minimize customer wait times and operational costs by ensuring failed deliveries are quickly re-allocated to the most suitable available agent.
rules: A failed delivery task must be reassigned only if at least one Delivery Partner is available within the defined service area.
The system must prioritize the Delivery Partner with the shortest estimated travel time to the delivery address.
Reassignment is prohibited if the selected Delivery Partner has exceeded their maximum capacity threshold for the current shift.
The original Delivery Partner must be notified of the task cancellation before the new assignment is finalized.

frs.requirement: The system shall reverse inventory locks and financial reservations for an Order Request when a cancellation is confirmed before the Fulfillment Task reaches the 'Ready for Dispatch' status.
frs.need: The business needs to ensure that cancelled orders do not permanently reduce available stock or hold customer funds, maintaining accurate inventory levels and financial integrity.
rules: Inventory locks must be released immediately upon confirmation of cancellation before the Fulfillment Task status changes to 'Ready for Dispatch'.
Financial reservations must be reversed only if the Order Request has not yet been handed over to a Delivery Partner.
A cancellation rollback cannot be initiated if the order has already been physically picked and verified by the Store Partner.
The system must validate that the Order Request ID matches the inventory lock ID before releasing stock.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable authorized agents and customers to upload photos and documents to substantiate dispute claims regarding delivery exceptions.
frs.need: The business needs a centralized mechanism to collect verifiable evidence to resolve disputes fairly and accurately.
rules: Only actors explicitly assigned to a Dispute Ticket may upload evidence for that specific ticket.
Uploaded evidence must be linked to the Order Request associated with the Dispute Ticket.
The system must prevent duplicate uploads of the same file for the same Dispute Ticket.
All uploaded evidence must be retained indefinitely for potential Regulatory Authority review.

frs.requirement: The system shall route unresolved disputes to senior support tiers based on calculated severity and financial impact thresholds.
frs.need: The business needs to ensure high-risk disputes receive immediate expert attention to minimize financial loss and maintain platform trust.
rules: A dispute must be escalated if the financial impact exceeds the standard liability limit.
A dispute must be escalated if fraud indicators suggest a high probability of fraudulent transaction.
Escalation must occur only after the initial support tier fails to resolve the issue within the standard timeframe.
The escalation path must strictly follow the hierarchy defined in the Store Partner Agreement.

frs.requirement: The system shall send real-time notifications to customers regarding the status updates of their refund requests.
frs.need: The business needs to maintain customer trust and reduce support volume by providing immediate transparency on refund processing stages.
rules: A notification must be sent immediately upon any change in the refund request status.
Notifications must only be sent if the new status differs from the status of the most recent notification.
The notification content must accurately reflect the current state of the Financial Transaction Record.
The system must verify the active communication channel exists before attempting to send a notification.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate high-risk transaction alerts and perform refund/chargeback impact analysis to prevent financial loss before settlement.
frs.need: The business needs to proactively identify fraudulent patterns and quantify potential financial exposure to stop unauthorized chargebacks before funds are settled.
rules: A transaction must be flagged if the calculated fraud likelihood score exceeds the configured risk threshold.
The projected financial impact must include the sum of item costs, delivery fees, taxes, and platform commissions.
A transaction must remain flagged until the Payment Provider confirms the outcome or the settlement period expires.
The impact analysis must be recalculated if new delivery proof or customer verification data becomes available.

frs.requirement: The system shall continuously reconcile platform revenue shares against store partner settlements in real-time.
frs.need: This ensures financial accuracy and trust between the platform and store partners by immediately identifying and resolving discrepancies in revenue distribution.
rules: A discrepancy is flagged if the calculated revenue share differs from the settlement amount by more than zero.
Reconciliation status must update to 'Resolved' only after the discrepancy is corrected and verified.
Revenue share calculations must strictly adhere to the commission rates defined in the active Store Partner Agreement.
Settlement amounts must include all applicable taxes, delivery fees, and platform commissions as per the Financial Transaction Record.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically compute and collect applicable taxes based on jurisdiction and product type during the order processing workflow.
frs.need: The business needs to ensure legal compliance and accurate revenue collection by dynamically applying the correct tax rates to every transaction.
rules: Tax must be calculated only on the subtotal of taxable items, excluding delivery fees and platform commissions.
The system must use the most current tax rate available for the specific jurisdiction at the time of order placement.
If a product is non-taxable in the delivery zone, the tax amount recorded must be zero.
The tax calculation must be reproducible using the same Order Request, Product Catalog, and Delivery Zone Map data.

frs.requirement: The system shall calculate and settle multi-currency transactions by converting amounts using real-time exchange rates and recording all financial details in the base currency of the Platform Operator.
frs.need: The business needs this to ensure accurate revenue collection and fair settlement for Store Partners and Delivery Partners regardless of the transaction's original currency.
rules: The system shall only allow currency conversion if the Store Partner Agreement explicitly permits transactions in the selected currency.
The system shall record the exchange rate used at the exact moment the Financial Transaction Record is created.
The system shall calculate the net settlement amount by subtracting the platform commission from the converted gross amount.
The system shall reject the transaction if the exchange rate source is unavailable or invalid.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate an immutable audit trail for every Financial Transaction Record and Settlement event to ensure financial integrity and regulatory compliance.
frs.need: The business requires a tamper-proof record of all monetary exchanges to resolve disputes, satisfy regulatory audits, and accurately calculate revenue shares.
rules: An audit log entry must be created immediately upon the finalization of a Financial Transaction Record status.
Any attempt to modify an existing audit log entry must be rejected and logged as a security violation.
The audit trail must include the full context of the Store Partner Agreement applicable to the transaction.
Audit logs must be accessible to the Regulatory Authority without requiring Platform Operator approval.

frs.requirement: The system shall execute a scheduled batch process to calculate, validate, and distribute financial settlements to Store Partners and Delivery Partners based on finalized transaction data.
frs.need: The business needs this to automate accurate fund distribution, ensuring partners receive correct payments while maintaining financial integrity and compliance with contractual agreements.
rules: A settlement batch must only include Order Requests where the Delivery Proof status is verified as successful.
The net settlement amount must be calculated strictly according to the active commission rates in the Store Partner Agreement.
Settlements cannot be processed if the associated Store Partner Agreement is expired or terminated.
Any discrepancy between the calculated settlement amount and the available Financial Transaction Record must trigger a batch halt for that specific item.
The system must exclude any Order Request flagged with high-risk indicators from the automated settlement batch.

frs.requirement: The system shall identify and flag suspicious financial patterns in financial transactions requiring manual review before settlement.
frs.need: The business needs this to prevent financial loss from fraud, reduce chargeback liabilities, and ensure accurate revenue settlement.
rules: A transaction is flagged if it exhibits unusual order patterns compared to the customer's historical behavior.
A transaction is flagged if it originates from a high-risk address or location not associated with the customer's profile.
A transaction is flagged if the payment method or amount deviates significantly from the customer's typical transaction profile.
Flagged transactions must remain in a pending state and cannot be settled until a Payment Provider manually approves or rejects them.

frs.requirement: The system shall dynamically adjust delivery fees and commissions based on real-time network congestion and predicted demand spikes.
frs.need: The business needs to balance network capacity with revenue optimization during high-demand periods to prevent service degradation.
rules: Surge pricing must only be applied when the ratio of active orders to available delivery agents exceeds the configured capacity threshold.
The system must not apply surge pricing if the predicted wait time for the customer exceeds the maximum acceptable delay defined in the Service Area Definition.
Adjusted fees must be calculated using the highest multiplier observed within the specific time window to ensure consistency.
Pricing adjustments must be communicated to the Customer Profile before the Order Request is finalized.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate predictive inventory replenishment alerts for high-velocity items when projected demand exceeds current stock levels within a defined time window.
frs.need: The business needs to notify store partners of impending stockouts for fast-moving items to prevent order fulfillment failures and maintain customer satisfaction.
rules: An alert must only be generated for items classified as high-velocity in the Product Catalog.
An alert is triggered only when the projected demand exceeds the current inventory by a defined safety margin.
Alerts must not be generated for items marked as temporarily unavailable in the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot.
The system must recalculate forecasts daily based on the latest Real-Time Inventory Snapshot.

frs.requirement: The system shall continuously recalculate optimal delivery paths for Delivery Partners by integrating live traffic data and new Order Request insertions.
frs.need: The business needs to minimize delivery times and fuel costs while ensuring timely order fulfillment in a dynamic logistics environment.
rules: A route must be recalculated whenever a new Order Request is inserted into an active zone.
Route optimization must prioritize the earliest Estimated Arrival Time for high-priority orders.
A Delivery Partner cannot be assigned a new task if their current workload exceeds the defined capacity threshold.
Reassigned routes must be communicated to the Delivery Partner within the maximum allowable notification latency.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically apply and track customer loyalty points or subscription benefits during the checkout and settlement process.
frs.need: The business needs to incentivize repeat purchases and retain customers by seamlessly integrating loyalty rewards into the transaction flow without manual intervention.
rules: A loyalty benefit cannot be applied if the Customer Profile indicates the account is suspended or flagged for fraud.
The net settlement amount must be recalculated immediately if the applied loyalty benefit exceeds the total order value, resulting in a zero or negative charge.
The system must prevent the application of loyalty benefits if the Order Request contains items restricted by the Store Partner Agreement.
The Customer Profile must be updated within the same transaction session to ensure the deducted balance is immediately reflected.

frs.requirement: The system shall provide real-time dashboards tracking delivery speed, accuracy, and customer satisfaction scores for each Delivery Partner.
frs.need: The business needs live visibility into agent performance to optimize workforce allocation, identify training gaps, and ensure consistent service quality across the network.
rules: A Delivery Partner's performance score must be updated immediately upon the submission of a Delivery Proof record.
Customer satisfaction scores must be weighted equally with delivery speed metrics in the overall performance calculation.
Performance data must be retained for a minimum period sufficient to generate weekly trend reports.
An agent's status must be flagged as 'Underperforming' if their average delivery time exceeds the zone standard for three consecutive shifts.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically monitor Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance for delivery times and order accuracy regarding Store Partners and alert the Fulfillment Supervisor upon breach.
frs.need: The business needs to proactively identify performance gaps to maintain contractual obligations and ensure customer satisfaction with delivery reliability.
rules: A delivery time breach occurs if the time between Order Request creation and Delivery Proof submission exceeds the agreed time window.
An order accuracy breach occurs if the items in the Delivery Proof do not match the Order Request specifications.
A breach notification must be generated immediately upon detection of any SLA violation.
The system must exclude force majeure events defined in the Store Partner Agreement from breach calculations.

frs.requirement: The system shall automatically generate and present retention incentives to customers identified as high-risk for churn based on negative feedback or service deviations.
frs.need: The business needs to proactively reduce customer attrition by offering targeted credits or offers immediately after detecting dissatisfaction signals.
rules: A retention offer must only be generated if the customer has at least one negative Feedback Record or an open Dispute Ticket.
The system must not generate a new retention offer for a customer if a valid offer is already active or pending redemption.
Retention offers must be automatically invalidated if the associated Dispute Ticket is resolved without a negative outcome.
The system must capture the specific reason code from the Feedback Record to determine the type of incentive offered.

frs.requirement: The system shall orchestrate multi-channel notifications (SMS, email, app push) by automatically triggering messages when an Order Request status changes to Ready for Delivery or Assigned to a Delivery Partner.
frs.need: The business needs to ensure customers receive timely, consistent updates across all preferred channels to reduce support inquiries and improve the delivery experience.
rules: A notification must only be triggered once per specific status transition event.
The notification channel must match the primary contact method defined in the Customer Profile.
If the primary contact method is unavailable, the system must attempt the secondary contact method.
Notifications must be sent within a maximum threshold of the status change timestamp.

frs.requirement: The system shall validate regulatory compliance and contractual terms to authorize new Store Partners for platform operations.
frs.need: The business needs this to ensure all partners operate legally within defined zones and adhere to agreed financial and service standards before accepting orders.
rules: A Store Partner cannot be activated until valid regulatory licenses are verified for the specific operating zone.
Operational access is restricted to partners whose locations fall strictly within an active Service Area Definition.
The system must reject onboarding requests where the Store Partner Agreement lacks defined performance guarantees or liability clauses.
Regulatory Authority must have the ability to override or suspend partner status based on compliance violations.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable customers to create, validate, and submit order requests containing selected items, quantities, and delivery instructions.
frs.need: This requirement ensures customers can accurately define their purchase needs and delivery preferences to initiate the fulfillment process.
rules: An Order Request cannot be submitted if any selected item is out of stock in the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot.
Delivery fees must be calculated based on the distance between the Store Partner and the delivery address within the Delivery Zone Map.
An Order Request is considered invalid if required customer contact information is missing or incomplete.
Special handling notes provided by the Customer must be stored and visible to the Fulfillment Supervisor during task assignment.

frs.requirement: The system shall route incoming order requests to the optimal Store Partner node and generate a corresponding Fulfillment Task for physical preparation and packing.
frs.need: The business needs to direct demand to the most efficient physical node to ensure timely order preparation and accurate inventory utilization.
rules: A Fulfillment Task must only be generated if the selected Store Partner has sufficient inventory for all items in the Order Request.
The assigned time window must allow the Store Partner to complete preparation before the delivery slot begins.
Stock reserved for a Fulfillment Task must be immediately reflected in the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot to prevent overselling.
If no Store Partner meets the optimal criteria, the system shall flag the Order Request for manual review by the Platform Operator.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable the Delivery Partner to execute the physical movement of goods from the Store Partner to the Customer and generate verifiable proof of delivery.
frs.need: The business needs to conclusively close the logistics loop by verifying successful handover and triggering financial settlement.
rules: A Fulfillment Task cannot be marked as completed without a valid Delivery Proof record.
The system must capture a timestamp and geolocation for every piece of Delivery Proof submitted.
The Delivery Partner must verify the specific list of items against the Order Request before generating proof.
Financial settlement is triggered only after the Delivery Proof is validated by the system.

frs.requirement: The system shall enable a Customer to submit a Feedback Record containing a satisfaction rating and textual comments after a Delivery Proof has been verified for a completed Order Request.
frs.need: The business needs this capability to collect qualitative data on product quality and service performance to drive operational improvements and evaluate partner effectiveness.
rules: A Feedback Record can only be created after a Delivery Proof exists for the associated Order Request.
The system must link the Feedback Record to the specific Delivery Proof to validate the context of the review.
Feedback submissions must include both a numerical rating and optional textual comments to be considered valid.
The system shall not allow duplicate feedback submissions for the same Order Request by the same Customer.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate demand forecasts and resource plans to optimize agent positioning and store inventory levels based on predicted order volumes.
frs.need: The business needs this to proactively allocate agents and stock before peak demand occurs, preventing service failures and reducing operational waste.
rules: The system shall only generate a resource plan if the predicted order volume exceeds the baseline threshold for the specific time window.
The system shall flag a Store Partner for immediate attention if the predicted demand exceeds 80% of their historical maximum capacity.
The system shall prioritize agent positioning recommendations for zones where predicted demand is rising faster than the average trend.
The system shall exclude Store Partners with a data link status indicating high latency or detected discrepancies from the resource plan.

frs.requirement: The system shall calculate a quality score for each Store Partner based on order preparation accuracy and customer feedback records.
frs.need: The business needs to objectively measure store performance to incentivize high-quality order preparation and identify partners requiring operational support.
rules: A Store Partner's quality score must be calculated only after at least three completed Fulfillment Tasks.
Negative feedback records regarding product quality must reduce the overall quality score.
The quality score must be recalculated whenever a new Feedback Record is submitted for a completed task.
Store Partners with scores below the minimum threshold must be flagged for review by the Fulfillment Supervisor.

frs.requirement: The system shall generate actionable quality improvement alerts when aggregated feedback data indicates systemic operational weaknesses.
frs.need: The business needs to proactively identify and address recurring service failures to maintain partner trust and operational efficiency.
rules: An alert is generated only if the same issue type appears in multiple Feedback Records within the defined time window.
Alerts must be categorized based on the primary sentiment of the associated textual comments.
A Feedback Record must be linked to a specific Delivery Assignment to validate the context of the quality issue.
Alerts for systemic issues must be prioritized higher than isolated single-instance feedback.

frs.requirement: The system shall route low-rated feedback records to a Fulfillment Supervisor for investigation and resolution actions.
frs.need: The business needs to proactively identify service failures to maintain customer trust and ensure fair resolution of disputes.
rules: A Feedback Record must be routed to a Fulfillment Supervisor if the rating is below the defined acceptable level.
A Dispute Ticket must remain open until a resolution status is recorded by the Fulfillment Supervisor.
The system must prevent the closure of a Feedback Record if the associated Dispute Ticket is still active.
Low-rated feedback must be included in the Platform Operator's quality assurance reports.

frs.requirement: The system shall aggregate feedback records to generate actionable insights for business strategy and operational improvement.
frs.need: The business needs to consolidate customer feedback to identify service weaknesses, evaluate partner performance, and drive quality improvements.
rules: A feedback record must contain both a quantitative rating and a qualitative comment to be included in aggregate reports.
Feedback records must be linked to a specific Delivery Assignment to attribute performance to the correct partner.
The system must categorize feedback into predefined service dimensions before aggregation.
Critical failure feedback must be prioritized and flagged for immediate supervisor review.

brs.name: Ultra-fast delivery of fresh perishables
brs.requirement: The business requires the capability to guarantee delivery of fresh perishables and daily essentials to customers within a 60-minute window.
brs.objective: This serves the core goal of meeting customer expectations for immediate gratification and reducing the friction of traditional grocery shopping.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement drives repeat usage and high ratings, while failure results in lost revenue and reputational damage due to spoiled goods or late arrivals.
policies: Compliance with local food safety and delivery regulations
Adherence to gig-economy labor laws for delivery partners

brs.name: Unified Digital Marketplace Interface
brs.requirement: The business requires a unified digital interface that aggregates fragmented inventory from multiple store partners to present a comprehensive assortment to customers.
brs.objective: This serves the goal of simplifying the shopping experience and enabling monetization through transaction commissions and advertising on a consolidated marketplace.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement increases customer retention and revenue; failure results in a fragmented user experience and lost sales opportunities.
policies: Inventory data must be synchronized in real-time to prevent overselling.
The interface must comply with data privacy regulations regarding customer location and purchase history.
Store partners must retain the right to define their own product categorization within the unified catalog.

brs.name: Optimize last-mile logistics via algorithmic routing
brs.requirement: The business requires an automated system to dynamically assign orders to gig workers and calculate optimal delivery paths to ensure efficient fulfillment and cost control.
brs.objective: Maintain profitability in a low-margin model while meeting strict time commitments required to satisfy the quick commerce promise.
brs.value: Meeting delivery targets ensures customer satisfaction and repeat usage, while dynamic routing minimizes operational costs and prevents order failures.
policies: Compliance with local gig-economy labor regulations regarding worker classification and pay transparency.
System must operate with low latency to support real-time decision-making during peak hours.
Routing algorithms must prioritize safety and avoid restricted zones defined by the Regulatory Authority.

brs.name: Measure orders fulfilled within target timeframes
brs.requirement: The business requires the Platform Operator to calculate and report the percentage of orders successfully delivered within the committed target window to validate service speed.
brs.objective: This requirement supports the core value proposition of ultra-fast delivery to drive customer retention and repeat usage.
brs.value: Meeting this metric ensures operational efficiency and maintains trust, while failure risks high churn and regulatory non-compliance regarding service level agreements.
policies: Metrics must align with the specific service area boundaries defined in the contract.
Data must be anonymized before sharing with external analytics partners.
Reports must be generated in real-time or near real-time.

brs.name: Track inventory discrepancies and overselling incidents
brs.requirement: The business requires continuous monitoring of inventory discrepancy rates and overselling incidents to ensure data accuracy and minimize order failures.
brs.objective: Maintain customer trust and prevent revenue loss from failed deliveries in a high-velocity environment.
brs.value: Accurate availability data reduces failed deliveries and protects revenue, while harm occurs if overselling leads to customer dissatisfaction and financial loss.
policies: Real-time synchronization is mandatory for perishable goods.
Discrepancies must be flagged immediately upon detection.
Data retention for discrepancy logs must comply with Regulatory Authority standards.

brs.name: Monitor revenue efficiency against operational costs
brs.requirement: The business requires a mechanism to continuously monitor the ratio of transaction commissions and delivery fees against operational costs to ensure profitability.
brs.objective: Sustaining the gig-economy logistics model requires rigorous cost control and optimization of multiple monetization channels to achieve positive unit economics.
brs.value: Ensures financial sustainability by identifying unprofitable orders or routes, while failure leads to eroding margins and potential service collapse.
policies: Financial data must be reconciled with Payment Provider records within 24 hours.
Operational cost data must be validated by the Fulfillment Supervisor before inclusion in reports.
Profitability metrics must exclude one-time setup costs for new Store Partners.

brs.name: Real-time Store Partner Performance Dashboard
brs.requirement: The business requires a transparent dashboard for Store Partners to view real-time order volume, revenue splits, and performance metrics.
brs.objective: Enable Store Partners to optimize staffing and inventory by understanding their individual financial contribution and operational performance.
brs.value: Improved partner retention and operational efficiency through data-driven decision-making; failure risks partner churn and inventory mismanagement.
policies: Data displayed must align with real-time settlement records per FR-039 and FR-005.
Performance metrics must be calculated using the quality scoring logic defined in FR-059.
Access to financial data is restricted to authorized Store Partner accounts only.

brs.name: Delivery Partner Financial Transparency Portal
brs.requirement: The business requires the platform to provide Delivery Partners with direct, secure access to their historical earnings summaries, payout schedules, and tax documents within the application interface.
brs.objective: This requirement supports the business goal of ensuring gig-economy worker financial compliance and trust, distinct from internal platform audit logging.
brs.value: Meeting this need reduces administrative friction for workers managing personal finances and mitigates reputational risk associated with tax non-compliance; failure to provide this harms worker retention and regulatory standing.
policies: Access to financial data must be restricted to authenticated Delivery Partners only.
All financial document downloads must be encrypted and logged for audit purposes.
Data retention for historical earnings must comply with local labor and tax laws.

brs.name: Customer Self-Service Loyalty and Subscription Portal
brs.requirement: The business requires a dedicated customer-facing portal enabling users to manage subscription preferences, view detailed delivery history, and access personalized loyalty rewards.
brs.objective: This requirement serves the goal of enhancing customer retention and increasing lifetime value through improved engagement and transparency.
brs.value: Meeting this need increases customer loyalty and reduces churn, while failure results in lower retention rates and diminished competitive advantage.
policies: Data privacy regulations must be strictly adhered to when displaying customer history.
The portal must integrate seamlessly with existing authentication systems.

brs.name: Dynamic Pricing Engine for Demand-Based Fees
brs.requirement: The business requires a dynamic pricing mechanism that adjusts delivery fees and commissions in real-time based on demand, weather, and traffic conditions.
brs.objective: This serves the goal of revenue optimization and Service Level Agreement (SLA) adherence during supply-demand fluctuations.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement maximizes revenue during peak times and ensures timely deliveries; failure results in lost revenue and breached delivery promises.
policies: Pricing adjustments must be transparent and communicated to the Customer before order confirmation.
Compliance with proposed Regulatory Authority guidelines on price discrimination and surge pricing disclosure.
Fee adjustments cannot exceed a proposed 200% of the base rate in any single transaction.

brs.name: Real-Time Inventory Reconciliation
brs.requirement: The business requires automated, real-time synchronization between physical store POS systems and the digital platform to prevent overselling and revenue leakage.
brs.objective: Ensure accurate inventory availability to maintain high customer satisfaction and prevent financial loss from uncollectible orders.
brs.value: Prevents failed deliveries and revenue leakage while ensuring regulatory compliance and operational efficiency.
policies: Must comply with local data privacy regulations regarding POS data integration.
Integration must not exceed 200ms latency during peak traffic hours.
System must support offline POS fallback with automatic sync upon reconnection.

brs.name: Continuous Financial Risk Mitigation
brs.requirement: The business requires continuous monitoring and mitigation of financial risks including fraud, chargebacks, and payment failures to protect cash flow and ensure settlement reliability.
brs.objective: This requirement serves the goal of operational sustainability and regulatory compliance in a high-volume, low-margin transaction model.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement prevents significant revenue loss and maintains trust, while failure leads to cash flow disruption and potential regulatory penalties.
policies: All financial settlements must comply with local regulatory authority standards.
Customer funds must be held in segregated accounts pending verification.
High-risk transactions require manual review before final settlement.

brs.name: Regulatory Compliance for Food Safety and Labor Laws
brs.requirement: The business requires strict adherence to external food safety standards and gig-economy labor laws to mitigate legal liability and operational risk.
brs.objective: Ensure the platform operates within legal boundaries to prevent fines, shutdowns, and reputational damage.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement protects the business from immediate legal action and ensures sustainable operations; failure results in severe financial penalties and loss of license.
policies: No Store Partner may operate on the platform without verified food safety certification.
All Delivery Partner contracts must explicitly comply with local gig-economy labor statutes.
Regulatory audits must be conducted quarterly by an independent third party.

brs.name: Proactive Risk Analytics for Brand Protection
brs.requirement: The business requires a predictive analytics capability that correlates delivery delays, inventory errors, and customer sentiment to proactively identify and mitigate threats to brand reputation and SLA performance.
brs.objective: This serves the goal of maintaining customer trust and retention in a low-margin, high-volume environment by shifting from reactive to proactive operational management.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement prevents brand equity erosion and customer churn caused by unaddressed operational friction, while failure results in reputational damage and lost revenue.
policies: Analytics must operate in real-time to enable immediate intervention.
Data usage must comply with all applicable privacy regulations.
Alerts must be actionable by the Fulfillment Supervisor within 15 minutes.

brs.name: Dynamic Tax Calculation and Collection
brs.requirement: The business requires the automatic calculation and collection of applicable taxes based on local jurisdiction rules and product types during order processing.
brs.objective: Ensure strict adherence to financial regulations and mitigate the risk of penalties from tax authorities.
brs.value: Prevents regulatory fines and maintains financial integrity, while harm arises from non-compliance and potential legal action.
policies: Tax rates must be updated in real-time to reflect local jurisdiction changes.
Calculations must be immutable and auditable for every transaction.
System must handle varying tax rules for different product categories.

brs.name: Mandatory Partner Compliance Validation
brs.requirement: The business requires a strict pre-onboarding validation process for all Store and Delivery Partners to verify regulatory licenses and contractual terms before operational access is granted.
brs.objective: This requirement ensures operational readiness by mitigating legal liability and supply chain disruptions caused by unverified partners.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement protects the business from regulatory fines and reputational harm, while non-compliance risks immediate service suspension and legal action.
policies: No partner may access the platform without a valid, verified license.
Contractual terms must be digitally signed and stored immutably.
Validation must occur prior to any order allocation or financial settlement.

brs.name: Rapid Isolation of System Outages
brs.requirement: The business requires the immediate containment of system failures or data corruption to prevent error propagation across the order lifecycle and protect revenue integrity.
brs.objective: This requirement serves the goal of maintaining high service availability and ensuring regulatory compliance during critical operational disruptions.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement prevents missed delivery windows, customer churn, and potential regulatory breaches, while failing to do so risks significant financial loss and reputational damage.
policies: Containment procedures must not compromise data integrity for active transactions.
Isolation mechanisms must comply with proposed regulatory data retention policies.
Rollback procedures must be validated by the Platform Operator before deployment.

brs.name: Guarantee immediate dispute resolution and fraud mitigation
brs.requirement: The business requires the immediate and transparent resolution of financial disputes and fraud attempts to maintain trust with Store Partners and Customers while minimizing revenue leakage.
brs.objective: Ensure financial integrity and regulatory compliance during high-volume micro-transaction settlement cycles.
brs.value: Failure to resolve disputes quickly erodes partner confidence and triggers regulatory scrutiny, leading to revenue loss and reputational damage.
policies: All financial settlements must be reconciled in real-time against store partner records.
Dispute resolution must adhere to local consumer protection and financial regulations.
Fraud detection must occur before order fulfillment to prevent loss.

brs.name: Immutable Audit Trail for Operational Anomalies
brs.requirement: The business requires a tamper-proof, immutable record of all operational anomalies to satisfy Regulatory Authority mandates and enable accurate root cause analysis during high-stakes investigations.
brs.objective: Mitigate legal liability and prove compliance regarding gig-worker labor laws and food safety standards.
brs.value: Failure to provide a verifiable record exposes the business to regulatory fines, legal action, and reputational damage, while success ensures operational transparency and trust.
policies: Audit logs must be cryptographically signed and stored on a write-once-read-many (WORM) storage system.
Access to raw anomaly data is restricted to authorized Platform Operator roles only.
Retention period for immutable records must align with proposed local jurisdiction laws.

brs.name: Dynamic Micro-Fulfillment Network Scaling
brs.requirement: The business requires the capability to dynamically scale its micro-fulfillment network and partner onboarding processes to maintain ultra-fast delivery SLAs during geographic expansion.
brs.objective: This requirement ensures that network complexity does not degrade the core value proposition of speed and reliability as the business enters new markets.
brs.value: Meeting this need prevents customer churn caused by service degradation, while failure risks losing market share to competitors with superior reliability.
policies: All new zones must achieve full regulatory compliance before operational activation.
Onboarding processes must not exceed proposed 48 hours for standard store partners.
Scaling must preserve the <60 minute delivery window for existing customers.

brs.name: Automated Quality Assurance and Dispute Resolution
brs.requirement: The business requires scalable, automated workflows to validate order quality and resolve disputes without manual intervention, ensuring consistent service standards as volume grows.
brs.objective: Protect brand reputation and maintain high customer satisfaction levels during periods of rapid order volume expansion.
brs.value: Prevents revenue loss from unresolved disputes and ensures consistent delivery quality, while reducing operational bottlenecks caused by manual oversight.
policies: All dispute workflows must comply with Regulatory Authority consumer protection guidelines.
Automated decisions must allow for human override by the Fulfillment Supervisor within 15 minutes.
Data used for quality scoring must be anonymized before sharing with Store Partners.

brs.name: Flexible Revenue and Settlement Management
brs.requirement: The business requires a dynamic financial framework that supports diverse partner commission structures, multi-currency transactions, and real-time reconciliation to sustain ecosystem profitability.
brs.objective: Enable scalable monetization and accurate financial settlement across a heterogeneous network of store and delivery partners.
brs.value: Ensures revenue integrity and partner trust while adapting to volatile market conditions and varying partner agreements.
policies: All settlements must comply with local financial regulations and tax laws.
Currency conversion must use real-time exchange rates from a designated source.
Revenue share logic must be auditable and immutable once finalized.

brs.name: Predictive Analytics for Demand and Inventory Optimization
brs.requirement: The business requires predictive analytics reports on demand patterns and inventory turnover to optimize resource allocation and reduce overselling incidents.
brs.objective: This requirement serves the goal of balancing supply with fluctuating demand to minimize operational waste and ensure high fulfillment accuracy.
brs.value: Meeting this need reduces inventory shrinkage and waste while improving customer satisfaction through accurate stock availability; failure results in overselling, financial loss, and reputational damage.
policies: Reports must be generated in real-time or near real-time to support immediate decision-making.
Data privacy regulations regarding customer purchase history must be strictly adhered to.
Analytics models must be auditable and explainable for regulatory compliance.

brs.name: Automated fallback routing and vendor diversification
brs.requirement: The business requires resilient order allocation capabilities that automatically switch to alternative logistics providers or mapping services when primary external dependencies fail.
brs.objective: This serves the goal of maintaining ultra-fast delivery promises and preventing revenue loss during third-party outages.
brs.value: If met, the business ensures continuous operations and customer trust; if not, service interruptions will lead to order cancellations and regulatory non-compliance.
policies: Failover logic must prioritize customer delivery timeframes over cost optimization.
Switching between providers must not require manual intervention by the Platform Operator.
System must log all fallback events for post-incident analysis by the Regulatory Authority.

brs.name: Third-Party Vendor SLA Enforcement
brs.requirement: The business requires legally binding Service Level Agreements with critical third-party vendors that mandate guaranteed uptime, rapid incident response, and financial penalties for service degradation.
brs.objective: Mitigate operational downtime and reputational damage caused by failures in external dependencies beyond the platform's direct control.
brs.value: Ensures service continuity and protects brand reputation by holding vendors accountable for performance, while preventing revenue loss from unavailability.
policies: All SLAs must include clear definitions of uptime and response metrics
Penalty clauses must be enforceable under local jurisdiction laws
Vendors must provide real-time status reporting interfaces

brs.name: Defer Advanced Predictive Inventory Models
brs.requirement: The business requires a strategic decision to postpone the development of advanced predictive inventory replenishment and complex demand forecasting models until sufficient historical transaction data is collected.
brs.objective: This serves the goal of minimizing initial development costs and technical debt while ensuring the platform launches with core, reliable functionality.
brs.value: Benefit includes faster time-to-market and reduced resource allocation; harm includes potential inefficiency in early inventory management if models are not yet mature.
policies: Core inventory validation must remain accurate without predictive features
Initial market data must be captured for future model training
No advanced forecasting features shall be marketed to partners pre-launch

brs.name: Proactive Perishable Inventory Management
brs.requirement: The business requires a mechanism to proactively manage perishable stock by generating real-time alerts for items approaching shelf-life limits to prioritize fulfillment or trigger removal.
brs.objective: This requirement serves the goal of minimizing product waste and maintaining quality standards to protect brand reputation and reduce loss costs.
brs.value: If met, the business reduces financial loss from unsellable goods and ensures customer satisfaction through high-quality deliveries; if not met, waste increases and customer trust erodes.
policies: Alerts must trigger before the item reaches its absolute expiration date.
Removal protocols must comply with local food safety regulations.
Inventory data must be synchronized in real-time across all Store Partners.

brs.name: Multi-channel delivery status notifications
brs.requirement: The business requires the Platform Operator to automatically send timely updates via SMS, email, or app push when an order status changes to Ready for Delivery or Assigned to a Delivery Partner.
brs.objective: This serves the goal of reducing support inquiries and improving the overall customer delivery experience through transparency.
brs.value: Meeting this requirement reduces customer frustration and support costs, while failure leads to increased complaints and lower retention.
policies: Notifications must comply with local telecommunications and data privacy regulations.
Messages must be sent within 2 minutes of the status change event.
Customers must be able to opt-out of non-critical promotional notifications.

actorsDetail.name: Payment Provider
actorsDetail.role: Financial institution that processes customer transactions and facilitates fund transfers.

actorsDetail.name: Fulfillment Supervisor
actorsDetail.role: Store staff member who coordinates the picking, packing, and handover of orders to delivery partners.

actorsDetail.name: Platform Operator
actorsDetail.role: Entity that manages the digital interface, orchestrates order allocation, and settles financial transactions.

actorsDetail.name: Customer
actorsDetail.role: End user who initiates orders, selects items, and confirms delivery completion.

actorsDetail.name: Delivery Partner
actorsDetail.role: Independent agent or gig-worker responsible for last-mile logistics and physical handover of goods.

actorsDetail.name: Store Partner
actorsDetail.role: Physical retail location that provides inventory, staff for order picking, and fulfillment capabilities.

actorsDetail.name: Order Allocation Engine
actorsDetail.role: Automated system component that validates inventory, calculates fees, and assigns orders to specific agents.

actorsDetail.name: Merchandiser
actorsDetail.role: Personnel at stores who pack orders and verify item quality before dispatch.

actorsDetail.name: Regulatory Authority
actorsDetail.role: External body that enforces food safety standards and labor laws applicable to the service.
